text:
Closest verified precedents differ from an explicit gate between GRU state hₜ and latest-item embedding eₜ. [NARM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.04725) concatenates the final GRU state with attention-pooled recurrent states; its local component is not the raw latest-item embedding. A more direct precedent, [US20210366025A1](https://patents.google.com/patent/US20210366025A1/en), projects [hₜ;eₜ] into one session representation—equivalently, an additive combination of learned projections. Its subsequent gate mixes current-session and neighbor-session representations, not hₜ and eₜ directly. Thus, combining recurrence with a latest-item shortcut has precedent; these sources do not establish an exact match for a proposed sigmoid output gate or justify a novelty claim.

Recommended mechanism ablations, rather than reported findings: independently retrain recurrent-only, last-item-only, ungated residual/concatenation, fixed-gate, and learned-gate variants under identical training and validation settings. Define “gate-only” explicitly: retain history-conditioned gating of eₜ but remove the direct recurrent value contribution, testing whether recurrence helps only through modulation. Also intervene on branches of the trained full model; distinguish these dependency probes from retrained ablations. Measure gate saturation and branch contribution norms, since gate values alone cannot establish reliance.

Evaluate recent-history lengths 1, 2, 5, 10 and full history; permute earlier items while preserving the final item, then separately permute all positions. [Residual Dominance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.14021) uses partial/full shuffling, includes GRU4Rec comparisons, and probes residual scaling, although its main mechanism concerns SASRec. Gains surviving earlier-history destruction but disappearing when the final item changes support latest-item reliance; improvements beyond last-item-only plus sensitivity to earlier-history order provide stronger evidence for useful recurrent context.
